domain.name: Procurement & Vendor Management
domain.description: Practical sourcing, vendor evaluation, purchasing workflows, contract administration, receiving, supplier performance, negotiation, and continuity planning.

competencies.name: Requirements & Sourcing
competencies.description: Translate a business need into clear sourcing requirements and a supplier search plan.
competencies.purpose: Prevent vague buying decisions and downstream rework.

units.title: Buy the requirement, not the pitch
units.content: Start with measurable needs, constraints, acceptance criteria, timing, ownership, and budget assumptions rather than vendor marketing language.

units.title: Sourcing workflow
units.content: Define need and must-haves; separate preferences; identify candidate suppliers; record assumptions; compare evidence consistently; document the decision.

units.title: Sourcing failures
units.content: Avoid choosing the first quote, changing requirements mid-comparison, hiding switching costs, and treating brand familiarity as proof of fit.

drills.title: Build a sourcing brief
drills.prompt: Create a vendor-search brief for a recurring business service.

competencies.name: RFQs, Quotes & Bid Comparison
competencies.description: Request and compare supplier quotes on an apples-to-apples basis.
competencies.purpose: Make price and scope differences visible before commitment.

units.title: RFQ structure
units.content: Use the same scope, quantities, service levels, due date, quote format, exclusions request, and decision timeline for every bidder.

units.title: Normalize before ranking
units.content: Convert quotes into comparable total-cost and scope views before deciding which is cheapest or best.

units.title: Quote comparison failures
units.content: Avoid comparing different scopes as if equivalent, ignoring taxes or setup fees, and assuming a low quote includes unstated work.

drills.title: Normalize three vendor quotes
drills.prompt: Build a comparison matrix for three quotes with different inclusions.

competencies.name: Purchase Orders & Receiving
competencies.description: Control the handoff from approved purchase to delivered goods or services.
competencies.purpose: Create a traceable record from request through receipt.

units.title: Three records should agree
units.content: Approved request, purchase order, and receipt or invoice should reconcile before a purchase is considered complete.

units.title: PO lifecycle
units.content: Confirm approval; issue exact order details; record vendor acknowledgment; track delivery; inspect receipt; document exceptions; close after reconciliation.

units.title: Receiving failures
units.content: Avoid paying against unverified delivery, changing quantities informally, accepting damaged goods without notation, and losing proof of receipt.

drills.title: Reconcile an order exception
drills.prompt: Resolve a delivery that arrived short against the PO and invoice.

competencies.name: Vendor Due Diligence & Risk
competencies.description: Evaluate supplier capability, reliability, security, concentration, and continuity risks.
competencies.purpose: Reduce dependency on weak or unsuitable vendors.

units.title: Due-diligence workflow
units.content: Verify identity and references; assess capacity, insurance or certifications when relevant, data access, subcontractors, continuity, and concentration risk; record evidence and open questions.

units.title: Risk follows access and dependency
units.content: A vendor with system access, customer data, sole-source status, or operational criticality needs more scrutiny than a low-value commodity supplier.

units.title: Due-diligence failures
units.content: Avoid collecting unnecessary sensitive data, relying on self-attestation alone for critical controls, and overlooking single-vendor dependency.

drills.title: Review a critical vendor
drills.prompt: Create a risk checklist for a vendor that will access business systems.

competencies.name: Contract & Scope Administration
competencies.description: Track commercial terms, scope, dates, deliverables, changes, and obligations without substituting for legal advice.
competencies.purpose: Keep agreed work and operational commitments visible.

units.title: Administration is not legal interpretation
units.content: Operational teams can track what a signed agreement says and when obligations are due; ambiguous legal meaning should be escalated to qualified counsel.

units.title: Contract administration workflow
units.content: Capture parties, term, renewal dates, scope, pricing, service levels, notice windows, owners, and approved changes; link evidence; schedule reviews.

units.title: Contract failures
units.content: Avoid oral scope expansion, missing renewal windows, changing material terms without authorization, and presenting legal conclusions as operational facts.

drills.title: Build a contract register
drills.prompt: Create an operational register for a vendor agreement.

competencies.name: Supplier Performance & Corrective Action
competencies.description: Measure delivery, quality, responsiveness, service levels, and recurring issues.
competencies.purpose: Improve vendor performance using evidence instead of anecdotes.

units.title: Scorecard workflow
units.content: Choose meaningful measures; collect consistent evidence; review trend and exceptions; discuss root causes; agree corrective action, owner, and due date.

units.title: Measure what affects outcomes
units.content: A short set of operational metrics tied to delivery and quality is better than a large scorecard nobody uses.

units.title: Performance failures
units.content: Avoid changing metrics after results appear, punishing one-off issues without context, and accepting repeated misses without documented action.

drills.title: Design a vendor scorecard
drills.prompt: Create a scorecard for a recurring service vendor.

competencies.name: Negotiation & Total Cost
competencies.description: Negotiate price, scope, timing, service, risk allocation, and total cost ethically.
competencies.purpose: Improve commercial outcomes without damaging supplier relationships.

units.title: Price is one variable
units.content: Total cost may include implementation, shipping, rework, downtime, support, minimums, payment timing, switching, and exit costs.

units.title: Negotiation preparation
units.content: Define target, walk-away, alternatives, must-haves, tradeable terms, evidence, and approval limits before negotiating.

units.title: Negotiation failures
units.content: Avoid bluffing about facts, making commitments outside authority, optimizing price while worsening risk, and negotiating without a fallback.

drills.title: Prepare a vendor negotiation
drills.prompt: Create a negotiation plan for a service renewal.

competencies.name: Supplier Continuity & Exit Planning
competencies.description: Prepare alternatives, transition plans, data return, inventory buffers, and replacement options for vendor failure or exit.
competencies.purpose: Reduce disruption when a supplier relationship changes.

units.title: Continuity workflow
units.content: Identify critical suppliers; define failure scenarios; record alternatives; preserve required documentation and data ownership; plan transition steps; test assumptions periodically.

units.title: Critical vendors need an exit before a crisis
units.content: The harder a supplier is to replace, the earlier continuity and offboarding should be designed.

units.title: Continuity failures
units.content: Avoid undocumented tribal knowledge, vendor-controlled credentials becoming sole access, and discovering export limitations only during termination.

drills.title: Create a vendor exit plan
drills.prompt: Plan the transition away from a critical software or service provider.
